wave: CORRECTNESS -- a single permission-denied subdirectory anywhere in the walked tree aborted the whole pipeline, the same defect class as the non-UTF-8 file-read crash, triggered by fs::read_dir instead of fs::read_to_string
wave_title: The immediately preceding generation (f5a8b7e3) fixed three `fs::read_to_string(...)?` call sites that crashed the whole pipeline on one unreadable FILE. A full audit of the same call sites' sibling `fs::read_dir(dir)?` calls -- `adapter::source::visit_inventory` (the whole repository's own source tree, the most consequential of the three), `adapter::visit_adl_sources`, and `adapter::visit_docs` -- found the identical defect for one unreadable DIRECTORY: `fs::read_dir` returns `Err(io::ErrorKind::PermissionDenied)` for a directory this process cannot list, and all three call sites propagated it via `?`, aborting the entire walk (every other artifact anywhere else in the repository) with zero report.

generation_model.G_n: f5a8b7e3bc (fix(adapter): a single non-UTF-8 file no longer aborts the whole pipeline) -- stable generation this candidate was built and validated against
generation_model.gap_discovered_by: Direct continuation of the immediately preceding generation's own audit method (grep every `fs::read_*` call site in production code for the crash-on-Err class already fixed twice this session), extended from `fs::read_to_string` to its sibling `fs::read_dir`. First reproduced the theory as root (this session's default execution context) via `chmod 000` on a scratch subdirectory -- and found it did NOT reproduce, because root bypasses discretionary directory-permission checks entirely on Linux (`fs::read_dir` on a `chmod 000` directory still succeeds for root). Rather than concluding 'no bug' from a negative result obtained under a privilege level that cannot exercise the check being tested (the same rigor this session already applied once before, ruling out a false-alarm symlink-cycle 'hang'), switched to the non-root `ubuntu` account already present in this container (`su ubuntu -c '...'`) and reproduced the real crash cleanly: `atlas-systemizer: /tmp/permtest/.atlas: Permission denied (os error 13)` with zero stdout, for a `docs audit` run against a repository with one unreadable subdirectory. Independently reproduced the same crash for `code analyze` against a permission-denied subdirectory inside a real `src/` tree (git itself printed 'could not open directory ... Permission denied' during `git add -A`, confirming this is an entirely ordinary, non-contrived real-world scenario, not a synthetic edge case).

priority_classification: correctness / hostile-and-degraded-environment handling (priority 1/2) -- the fourth instance this session of the same underlying defect class (one artifact's or subtree's io::Error aborting the entire pipeline instead of a typed, partial report), and the most consequential of the four: `visit_inventory` walks the ENTIRE repository source tree, not just `.atlas`, so any permission-restricted subdirectory anywhere in a real repository (a common, unremarkable occurrence -- build caches, credential directories, vendored tools with restrictive permissions) previously made Atlas unable to produce any report at all.

design_decisions.question: The unit-test suite in this session's own environment runs as root, which bypasses the exact permission check this fix targets -- ship an untestable-in-this-environment fix, skip it, or find another way to verify?
design_decisions.decision: Ship the fix (verified via real, non-root process execution: `su ubuntu -c '.../atlas-systemizer ...'`, both before the fix -- confirmed crash -- and after -- confirmed graceful handling) AND add a real `#[cfg(unix)] #[test]` that exercises the same scenario with `chmod 000`, guarded by a root-detection check (`/proc/self/status`'s `Uid:` line -- avoiding a new `libc` dependency for one environment probe) that prints a clear skip message and returns early only when running as root. This is not a placeholder: on any standard non-root CI (the overwhelmingly common case for a Cargo test suite) the test fully exercises the real regression; in this session's own root sandbox it correctly and visibly declines to produce a false pass rather than silently asserting something it cannot actually verify.

design_decisions.question: How to account for the unreadable directory in `visit_inventory` specifically, versus the best-effort silent skip used for `visit_adl_sources`/`visit_docs`?
design_decisions.decision: `visit_inventory` already has a rich, structured accounting channel for exactly this situation -- `ArtifactRecord`/`classify_non_file`, the same mechanism already used for a symlink or a special (non-file/non-dir) filesystem entry -- so the unreadable directory is recorded through it: `ArtifactKind::Special`, `ArtifactDisposition::Unknown` (distinct from `Unsupported`, which the existing symlink/special-file cases use to mean 'we know what this is, we simply don't parse it' -- `Unknown` correctly means 'we cannot even determine what this contains'), with a `reason` string carrying the real OS error message for diagnosability. `visit_adl_sources`/`visit_docs` have no equivalent per-directory accounting channel (same constraint the immediately preceding generation already accepted for their non-UTF-8 file-read fix), so they get the same best-effort 'skip, don't crash' treatment as before -- consistent scope, not a regression from the richer treatment `visit_inventory` receives.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: A subdirectory this process cannot list (permission denial being the common real case, but any `read_dir` failure handled identically) anywhere in a repository's source tree, `.atlas/declared/` tree, or `.atlas` docs tree no longer aborts `systemize`/`code_analyze`/`docs audit`/`check`/`parse`/`work prepare`. In the source tree specifically, the unreadable directory is recorded as an explicit `ArtifactRecord` (kind `SPECIAL`, disposition `UNKNOWN`, reason naming the real OS error) rather than silently dropped, and every other artifact in the repository is still inventoried normally.
stable_validator_law_compliance.self_written_evidence: New `#[cfg(unix)]` regression test `an_unreadable_subdirectory_is_recorded_not_walked_and_does_not_abort_the_rest_of_the_tree` in `adapter/src/source/mod.rs`, using a real `chmod 000` directory, guarded by a root-detection skip (confirmed to correctly detect and skip in this session's own root environment, via `--nocapture` showing the skip message).
stable_validator_law_compliance.independent_evidence_channel: Real, rebuilt `atlas-systemizer` binary invoked as the non-root `ubuntu` account (`su ubuntu -c '...'`) against two independently-constructed scratch repositories: one with a permission-denied subdirectory under `.atlas` (`docs audit`: previously `exit 2`, 'Permission denied (os error 13)', zero stdout; now `exit 2` with the expected, unrelated `DOCS_GATE_NOT_READY` business-logic exit and a full valid report), and one with a permission-denied subdirectory under a real `src/` tree, discovered via ordinary `git add -A` (`code analyze`: previously crashed identically; now exit 0, correctly listing `Cargo.toml`/`src/lib.rs` while recording `src/locked` as `{"kind": "SPECIAL", "disposition": "UNKNOWN", "reason": "directory-not-readable: Permission denied (os error 13)"}`). Full workspace re-run (`cargo fmt --all --check`, `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, `cargo test --workspace`) and a fresh `systemize` run against the real Atlas-Studio repository itself confirm zero regression to any existing gate, blocker, or test.

implementation.adapter/src/source/mod.rs: New `record_unreadable_directory` helper (records `dir` itself as an `ArtifactRecord` with kind `Special`/disposition `Unknown` instead of propagating the `io::Error`). `visit_inventory`'s `fs::read_dir(dir)?` and its subsequent `.collect::<Result<_,_>>()?` both changed from `?`-propagation to explicit `match` arms that call this helper and return `Ok(())`. New root-detection helper `running_as_root` (`/proc/self/status`-based, no new dependency) and new `#[cfg(unix)]` regression test.
implementation.adapter/src/lib.rs: `visit_adl_sources` and `visit_docs`'s `fs::read_dir(dir)?` calls both changed to `let Ok(..) = fs::read_dir(dir) else { return Ok(()); }` (best-effort skip, matching the accounting-channel constraint already accepted for these two functions' non-UTF-8 file-read fix last generation).

this generation closes the read_dir sibling of the read_to_string defect class the immediately preceding generation closed, completing the sweep across every recursive filesystem walk in adapter/src (source inventory, ADL sources, docs) for both 'a file's bytes could not be decoded' and 'a directory could not be listed' -- the same discipline runtime::census::extraction::extract_semantics already established for its own per-artifact read failures now applies consistently to every repository-content-reading call site in the codebase
the root-detection test-skip pattern (`/proc/self/status`-based) introduced here is reusable for any future permission-dependent regression test in this codebase, without adding a new dependency
overall_verdict: MATERIALIZED AND VERIFIED. A single permission-denied (or otherwise unreadable) subdirectory anywhere in a repository's source tree, declared-ADL tree, or docs tree previously aborted the entire pipeline with zero report -- the read_dir sibling of the read_to_string defect class fixed in the immediately preceding generation, and the most consequential of the two since it affects the whole source tree, not just .atlas. Fixed at all three call sites; the source-tree case is now explicitly accounted for as an ArtifactRecord (never silently dropped) rather than merely skipped. Verified with a real, non-root, falsification-first end-to-end reproduction (crash captured against the unfixed code before any fix was written) plus a root-detection-guarded unit regression test, with zero regression to the real repository's own state or any existing test.
